claims: Gary Woodland underwent brain surgery to remove a tumor in September 2023.
Gary Woodland has battled severe PTSD, anxiety, and fear following September 2023 brain surgery.
Gary Woodland openly shared in March 2026 that despite returning to the PGA Tour, he struggled with mental fatigue, panic, and felt like he was "dying inside" while competing.
Gary Woodland's tumor was on the part of his brain controlling fear and anxiety.
Post-surgery, Gary Woodland suffered from fear of dying and intense, recurring anxiety.
Gary Woodland returned to play in early 2024.
Despite returning to play in early 2024, Gary Woodland hid the severity of his mental battle.
Gary Woodland often cried in the scoring trailer or his car.
Gary Woodland experienced intense, overwhelming symptoms at the 2024 Procore Championship.
Gary Woodland experienced memory issues at the 2024 Procore Championship.
Gary Woodland was easily startled at the 2024 Procore Championship.
The 2026 Texas Children’s Houston Open was Gary Woodland's first win since the surgery.
Gary Woodland won the 2026 Texas Children’s Houston Open just weeks after publicly revealing the depth of his PTSD struggle
